userStories.title: The session role claim comes from bindings
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Derive session, profile and assistant user roles from bindings instead of User.role while preserving response contracts.

**Motivation** — The JWT `role` claim, `UserPrincipal.role` and `UserResponseDto.role` (login, register, refresh, invite acceptance, `GET /auth/me`) are read from the `User.role` column, so they are only as right as the mirror.

**Approach** — `AuthService` gains two methods and changes one:

- `roleClaim(userId: string): Promise<KodaUserRole>` answers `'ADMIN'` when `MembershipService.isGlobalAdmin(userId)` resolves `true`, else `'MEMBER'`.
- `userResponse(user: UserDomain): Promise<UserResponseDto>` answers `UserResponseDto.from(user, await this.roleClaim(user.id))`.
- `issueSession(user: UserDomain)` becomes `async` and answers `Promise<AuthResponseDto>`: it signs the access token with `roleClaim(user.id)` and returns `user: await this.userResponse(user)`.

`AuthController.me` maps the validated user through `authService.userResponse(validatedUser)` instead of `UserResponseDto.from(validatedUser)`. `InviteAcceptanceService.accept` awaits `this.auth.issueSession(user)`.

**Registration re-reads the user.** `AuthService.register` issues the session from `authRepo.findUserById(created.id)` read after the registration transaction committed, not from the row `findAnyUserAndCreate` returned. Once the first-user write stops storing `role: 'ADMIN'`, the Owner binding `bindOwnerIfFirst` writes is a flip (ruling 2) and bumps `tokenVersion` inside the transaction, so a token signed with the pre-bump `tokenVersion` would be revoked on its first use.

`PrismaAuthRepository` stops reading and writing the column: `toDomain` has no `role`, `createUser` takes no `role`, and `findAnyUserAndCreate` writes `data` as given for the first user too. `PrismaProjectInvitesMembersRepository.createInvitedUser` writes and returns no `role`.

The assistant's user principal (`userPrincipal` in `assistant-tool.executor.ts`) keeps reading `creator.role`; `PrismaAssistantToolCallRepository.findUserActor` derives that `role` with ruling 1, reading the user's global `owner`/`admin` binding count from `roleBinding` in the same repository (as `PrismaUsersRepository.countActiveAdmins` already reads `roleBinding`), and stops selecting the `role` column.

The derived role: A user's role claim is `'ADMIN'` when the user holds at least one binding with `principalType` `USER`, `projectId` null and role key `owner` or `admin`; otherwise it is `'MEMBER'`. A `project-admin` binding, in one project or in all projects (`projectId` null with a PROJECT-scope role), does not make it `'ADMIN'`. The claim decides nothing (`.nax/rules/api-auth.md`, "No Decisions on Role Claims"); it is display and compatibility data.

Failure handling: `MembershipService.isGlobalAdmin` rejects while a session is issued (login, register, refresh, invite accept): the error propagates; no token is signed. Resolve the claim lookup and userResponse successfully before signing either token, so even a rejection from userResponse's role lookup cannot occur after a token was already signed.

**Scope** — In: UserDomain role removal, DTO mapping signature, async session consumers, auth/invite-account repository cleanup, assistant actor derivation, and the specs this first breaks. Out: replacing MembershipService's mirror/revocation algorithm (US-002), remaining user/invite column writes and physical drops (US-003), legacy tables (US-004), CLI/web display changes (US-005/006); do not remove compatibility claims or regenerate contracts.

**Interface** — `AuthService.issueSession(user: UserDomain): Promise<AuthResponseDto>`; `AuthService.roleClaim(userId: string): Promise<KodaUserRole>`; `AuthService.userResponse(user: UserDomain): Promise<UserResponseDto>`; `UserResponseDto.from(user: UserDomain, role: KodaUserRole)`; `PrismaAuthRepository.createUser(data: { email: string; name: string; passwordHash: string })`; `UserToolCallCreator.role: KodaUserRole`. `UserDomain` has no `role` field.

**Verification** — Use strict three-session TDD. Create test/integration/auth/role-claim-from-bindings.integration.spec.ts; update auth.service.spec.ts with isGlobalAdmin, awaited session behavior and post-commit findUserById; controller me stubs userResponse; repository tests expect only given create data and no returned domain role; invite acceptance uses an async issueSession double and no account role; assistant-action-actor.integration.spec.ts proves derived MEMBER/ADMIN. Initially ACs 4/13 deliberately seed stored ADMIN to demonstrate that it grants no claim; US-003 later removes those column writes but preserves their MEMBER assertions. Run API scoped unit/integration tests with seeded system roles and a real test Postgres; keep existing refusal cases unchanged.

userStories.title: Token revocation follows global-admin bindings
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Replace the User.role mirror with token-version bumps exactly on binding-derived ADMIN/MEMBER flips.

**Motivation** — Nothing decides on the legacy tables, but they still exist and are still written: `PrismaAuthRepository.findAnyUserAndCreate` stores `role: 'ADMIN'` for the first user, `UsersAdminService.create` and `PrismaProjectInvitesMembersRepository.createInvitedUser` store `role: 'MEMBER'`, `ProjectInvitesService.inviteNewAddress` stores the legacy enum in `ProjectInvite.role`, and `MembershipService` mirrors every global `owner`/`admin` binding into `User.role` through `PrismaRoleBindingRepository.setUserRole`.

**Approach** — `PrismaRoleBindingRepository.setUserRole(userId, role)` is replaced by `bumpTokenVersion(userId: string): Promise<boolean>`: one `user.updateMany({ where: { id: userId }, data: { tokenVersion: { increment: 1 } } })`, answering `count > 0`.

In `MembershipService`:

- `insertBinding`, for a `USER` principal, `projectId` null and a role key in `GLOBAL_ADMIN_ROLE_KEYS`, reads `countGlobalAdminBindings(userId)` after the locks and the `findExisting` check and before `createBinding`; when it was `0`, it calls `bumpTokenVersion(userId)` and lists the user in `revokedUserIds` when that answers `true`. An existing identical binding (the `findExisting` early return) bumps nothing.
- `afterRemoval` keeps its candidate set (users whose removed bindings include a global `owner`/`admin` one); `syncLegacyRole` becomes `revokeIfNoGlobalAdmin(userId)`: when `countGlobalAdminBindings(userId)` is `0` it calls `bumpTokenVersion(userId)` and answers its result, else `false`.
- `setGlobalAdmin(userId, false, by)` (no production caller; kept) revokes only when it deleted the user's global `admin` binding (`existing !== null`) and `countGlobalAdminBindings(userId)` is then `0`; when it deleted nothing it bumps nothing, as today's `setUserRole` changed nothing for a plain member.
- `afterWrite` is unchanged: it invalidates the two cache entries of each `revokedUserIds` user after commit.

`PrismaRoleBindingRepository.findUserState` selects only `disabled` and answers `UserAccountState` (`{ disabled: boolean }`), which replaces `UserLegacyState` in `permissions.types.ts`. `InMemoryPermissionStore` follows: users are `{ disabled, tokenVersion }`, `addUser(id, disabled = false)`, and `bumpTokenVersion` increments `tokenVersion` and pushes `tokens:<userId>` onto `store.calls`; a `bumpTokenVersionFailure: Error | null` field makes the next call reject, like `openAgentTicketsFailure`.

Revocation follows the flip. A binding write revokes a user's tokens (bumps `tokenVersion`, then drops `userTokenVersionCacheTag(userId)` and `userAuthStateCacheKey(userId)` after commit) exactly when it changes that user's derived role: an insert of a global `owner`/`admin` binding for a user who held none, and a removal that leaves a user with none. This replaces "every change of `User.role` bumps `tokenVersion`" in the design doc's notes; the lock order of `MembershipService` (the `owner` Role row, then the user row) is unchanged. Only USER/null/owner-or-admin bindings affect the derived role; PROJECT-scope roles never promote the claim even with projectId null.

Failure handling: `bumpTokenVersion` rejects inside a binding write: the error propagates and the binding write's transaction rolls back. `bumpTokenVersion` finds no user row: answers `false`; the user is not listed in `revokedUserIds`.

**Scope** — In: production mirror replacement, account-state type, in-memory store and failure injection, all existing specs first broken by those interfaces, and EVERY assertion on stored User.role, including assertions fixture mirrors or defaults would keep green. Out: physical column drops and remaining account/invite writes (US-003), fixture grant mirror removal (US-003), removeProjectBindings/deleteProjectBindings deletion and table/report cleanup (US-004), session producers (US-001), CLI/web changes (US-005/006). US-002 only: a test that races two concurrent global `owner`/`admin` grants of one user is out of scope; the user-row lock `insertBinding` takes before the count serializes them, and the existing B2 case exercises that lock.

**Interface** — `PrismaRoleBindingRepository.bumpTokenVersion(userId: string): Promise<boolean>`; `PrismaRoleBindingRepository.findUserState(userId: string): Promise<UserAccountState | null>`; `UserAccountState = { disabled: boolean }`; `InMemoryPermissionStore.addUser(id: string, disabled = false)`; `bumpTokenVersionFailure: Error | null`. `setUserRole` and `UserLegacyState` are removed.

**Verification** — Strict three-session TDD: create src/permissions/membership.service.token-revocation.spec.ts for service/double/repository cases and test/integration/permissions/global-admin-token-revocation.integration.spec.ts for grants/removals through /role-bindings and old-token /auth/me probes. Preserve B2 lock coverage, owner protections and after-commit invalidation. Update membership.service, removal-guards, role-matrix, role-admin and permission.service unit specs for addUser and binding-backed admins. Replace integration mirror assertions with exact tokenVersion deltas in membership-service/role-bindings-api; replace registration/admin-user role counts with enabled binding-holder counts; remove redundant stored-role assertions across notification, seed, fixture, project, fleet and VCS cases without weakening their binding/recipient assertions. A legacy-admin-with-no-binding setGlobalAdmin(false) case now proves no bump. Keep newUser(role) DB helpers and all role writes until US-003. Keep removeProjectBindings tests until US-004, but remove their stored-role assertions now. Run bun run --cwd apps/api type-check and bun run --cwd apps/api lint as removal verification, plus real DB scoped tests; these commands are not ACs.

userStories.title: Drop User.role and ProjectInvite.role
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Physically drop the two legacy role columns and remove remaining column-dependent API, fixture, seed and spec code.

**Motivation** — About 80 DB-backed specs still write `role` on user rows, assert the stored `User.role`, or seed and count legacy rows.

**Approach** — Migration `20261102090000_drop_legacy_role_columns`:

```sql
-- Permissions P1m US-003: the role claim is derived from role bindings, and an invite names its role by roleId.
ALTER TABLE "User" DROP COLUMN "role";
ALTER TABLE "ProjectInvite" DROP COLUMN "role";
```

`schema.prisma` loses `User.role` and `ProjectInvite.role`. Then, per file:

| File | Change |
|:--|:--|
| `src/users/domain/user-admin.domain.ts` | `GLOBAL_ROLES`, `GlobalRole`, `UserAdminRecord.role` and `UserAdminWrite.role` go |
| `src/users/prisma-users.repository.ts` | `toRecord` has no `role`; `createUser(data: { email; name; passwordHash })`; `updateUser` writes no `role` |
| `src/users/users-admin.service.ts` | `create` passes no `role` |
| `src/projects/invites/domain/project-invite.domain.ts` | `ProjectInviteRecord.role` goes; `roleKey` / `roleName` come from `roleId` only |
| `src/projects/invites/prisma-project-invites.repository.ts` | `CreateProjectInviteInput.role` goes and `create` writes no `role`; `legacyRoleNames` goes; `toRecord` answers `roleKey: row.assignedRole?.key ?? null` and `roleName: row.assignedRole?.name ?? null` |
| `src/projects/invites/project-invites.service.ts` | `legacyNameOf` goes; the invite mail `role` is `invite.roleName ?? ''` |
| `src/tickets/prisma-tickets.repository.ts`, `src/tickets/domain/ticket.domain.ts` | `findUserById` selects and answers `{ id, disabled }` |
| `src/permissions/test-helpers/permission-fixtures.ts` | `grantRole` writes only the binding (the `mirrorsAdmin` user update goes); `fixtureGrantReport` reads no `role` (`legacyMemberships` counts `ProjectMember` rows only) |
| `prisma/seed.ts` | prints `outcome.roleKey` for a created admin, and no role for an existing email |

An invite whose `roleId` is null (its custom role was deleted) names no role: it lists with `roleKey` and `roleName` null and its acceptance answers 409 `invites.roleGone`, as `InviteAcceptanceService.invitedRole` already does for a row with neither.

One migration per legacy object group. US-003 drops the two columns (`User.role`, `ProjectInvite.role`) in `20261102090000_drop_legacy_role_columns`; US-004 drops the three tables in `20261102090100_drop_legacy_membership_tables`. No data is copied (design decision 2). Each migration ships with a scratch-schema test in the pattern of `test/integration/fleet/pending-action-drop-legacy-columns-migration.integration.spec.ts` (`scratchSchemaBefore`, `applyMigration` from `test/helpers/migration-schema.ts`).

Failure handling: an invite whose roleId is null answers 409 invites.roleGone and creates no user and no binding; legacy columns and their values are dropped while every other row is kept. No API contract change. `UserResponseDto` keeps `role`; no route, DTO or response field changes, so `openapi.json` and `apps/cli/src/generated/` are not regenerated.

**Scope** — In: this exact column migration, Prisma schema/client regeneration, column-dependent domain/repository/service/fixture/seed removal, and all user/invite role writes in specs. Out: dropping ProjectMember/AgentProject/AgentRoleEntry and report table fields (US-004), changing the completed session/revocation algorithms (US-001/002), CLI/web changes (US-005/006). Keep legacy-project-roles.ts and its display vocabulary; keep compatibility claims and mail's display role; do not backfill legacy data or regenerate contracts.

**Interface** — `PrismaUsersRepository.createUser(data: { email: string; name: string; passwordHash: string }): Promise<UserAdminRecord>`; `TicketsRepository.findUserById(id: string): Promise<{ id: string; disabled: boolean } | null>`; `ProjectInviteRecord` has no `role` field.

**Verification** — Strict three-session TDD. Author drop-legacy-role-columns-migration.integration.spec.ts using scratchSchemaBefore(baseUrl, schema, target), raw SQL to seed prior-schema User/ProjectInvite rows, applyMigration and schema-scoped information_schema queries; the helper starts BEFORE target. Assert preserved id/email/tokenVersion/disabled and roleId/status/tokenHash. Update unit expectations in users-admin.service, project-invites.service, prisma-project-invites.repository and project-invite.domain; remove stale typed UserAdminRecord.role fixtures wherever the removed domain field breaks them. Replace fallback-invite acceptance tests with null-roleId 409 behavior, retaining existing roleId/roleKey assertions. Sweep DB user/invite role writes across the specified auth, agents, fleet, permissions, projects and tickets suites, including the upstream role-claim-from-bindings file. Remove role parameters from newUser/createUser helpers and grant actual admin bindings when access is needed. roles-api/membership-queries principals and the thread-creator-type expected actor role use literal MEMBER; preserve older scratch-schema raw INSERTs. grantRole regression must keep tokenVersion unchanged, unlike production grants; ticket assignment regression must keep the assigned enabled developer's id. Do not remove legacy-table setups/counts until US-004, and do not edit mock-only legacy delegate proofs. Run bun run --cwd apps/api db:generate, then bun run --cwd apps/api type-check and bun run --cwd apps/api lint; run affected DB specs through test:scoped with real Postgres.

The replacing invariant: rows and records carry no role, create writes none, and a row without an assigned role answers roleKey and roleName null.

userStories.title: Drop ProjectMember, AgentProject and AgentRoleEntry
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Drop the remaining legacy membership tables and remove their unused CRUD/membership methods, legacy fixture-report fields and DB-spec dependencies, retaining the assignee repository's search interface.

**Motivation** — `PrismaProjectAssigneesRepository` is still built on the `ProjectMember` model, `PrismaProjectInvitesMembersRepository.createMember` still writes a `ProjectMember` row (no caller), and `MembershipService.removeProjectBindings` has had no production caller since PR #322.

**Approach** — Migration `20261102090100_drop_legacy_membership_tables`:

```sql
-- Permissions P1m US-004: memberships, agent rosters and agent roles are role bindings.
DROP TABLE "ProjectMember";
DROP TABLE "AgentProject";
DROP TABLE "AgentRoleEntry";
```

`schema.prisma` loses the three models and the relation fields that name them: `User.projectMemberships`, `User.addedAgentProjects`, `Agent.roles`, `Agent.projects`, `Project.members`, `Project.agents`. Then:

- `PrismaProjectAssigneesRepository` stops extending `AbstractPrismaRepository<ProjectMembershipDomain, ProjectMember, string>`: it is a plain `@Injectable()` class with the constructor's `PrismaService` and its one method `search` (unchanged). `IProjectAssigneesRepository` no longer extends `IRepository<ProjectMembershipDomain, string>`, and `ProjectMembershipDomain` goes. The CRUD half had no caller; `ProjectAssigneesService` calls only `search`. The `PROJECT_ASSIGNEES_REPOSITORY` token and its module wiring stay.
- `PrismaProjectInvitesMembersRepository.createMember` goes.
- `MembershipService.removeProjectBindings`, `PrismaRoleBindingRepository.deleteProjectBindings`, the in-memory double's `deleteProjectBindings` and the `GlobalStubsModule` stub `removeProjectBindings` go (ruling 2026-10-23).
- `fixtureGrantReport` answers `FixtureGrantReport` with `hasGlobalBinding` and `globalProjectRoleBindings` only; `legacyMemberships` and `agentRoleEntries` go.
- `seedE2e`'s `wipe` drops the `agentRoleEntry.deleteMany()` line.

One migration per legacy object group. US-003 drops the two columns (`User.role`, `ProjectInvite.role`) in `20261102090000_drop_legacy_role_columns`; US-004 drops the three tables in `20261102090100_drop_legacy_membership_tables`. No data is copied (design decision 2). Each migration ships with a scratch-schema test in the pattern of `test/integration/fleet/pending-action-drop-legacy-columns-migration.integration.spec.ts` (`scratchSchemaBefore`, `applyMigration` from `test/helpers/migration-schema.ts`).

Failure handling: when a migration runs on a database that holds legacy rows, the legacy tables and their rows are dropped; every other row is kept. Keep the exact migration order after US-003 and do not perform a backfill.

**Scope** — In: the exact table migration and schema relations, unused CRUD/membership methods and stubs, fixture report and its consumers, e2e seed wipe, and specs seeding/counting the removed tables. Out: changing assignee search behavior or token/module wiring, changing completed column/session/revocation work (US-001/002/003), CLI/web changes (US-005/006). Keep legacy-project-roles.ts display vocabulary, ProjectMemberRole/AgentRoleNames/KodaAgentRole types and comments mentioning historical tables. Mock-only delegate specs are excluded, and old migration/scratch-schema SQL retains legacy names.

**Interface** — `IProjectAssigneesRepository` — Target: `{ search(projectId, q, limit, ids): Promise<AssigneeDomain[]> }`, not an `IRepository`. `FixtureGrantReport` — Target: `{ hasGlobalBinding: boolean; globalProjectRoleBindings: number }`. `PrismaProjectAssigneesRepository` receives only PrismaService; `ProjectMembershipDomain`, `createMember`, `removeProjectBindings` and `deleteProjectBindings` are removed.

**Verification** — Strict three-session TDD. Create drop-legacy-membership-tables-migration.integration.spec.ts with scratchSchemaBefore, seed one legacy row per table plus referenced User/Agent/Project and a RoleBinding through raw SQL, applyMigration, and inspect schema-scoped table absence and preserved records. US-003 already removed User.role in this scratch schema. Update the assignee repository unit constructor without altering search cases; preserve DB-free module-token coverage. Delete membership.service.spec.ts's removeProjectBindings block, matching in-memory/global-stub members and project-members service doubles/assertions; remove createMember from invite acceptance doubles. Adjust expectBindingOnlyFixtures and stale report exemptions to consume only the two surviving report invariants. Sweep endpoint.e2e.spec.ts and DB integration suites in agents, email, fleet, memory, permissions, projects, rag, skills and vcs: remove obsolete legacy zero-count assertions, helpers and legacy-only cases, retaining or replacing meaningful behavior assertions with RoleBindings. In permissions retain binding query/access/roster/ticket/recipient cases; in endpoint e2e assert actual agent/member bindings or keep response assertions. permission-fixtures stops deleting legacy delegates and expects only the two report fields. Verify unchanged assignee ordering and two seedE2e runs. Preserve fixtureGrantReport's missing-user negative path, returning exactly the surviving two-field base report { hasGlobalBinding: false, globalProjectRoleBindings: 0 }. Run bun run --cwd apps/api db:generate, then bun run --cwd apps/api type-check and bun run --cwd apps/api lint, plus affected real-Postgres scoped tests. Do not edit generated OpenAPI/client code or mock-only legacy delegate specs.
